speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
Good evening, everyone. Well, we’ll take  a short few questions. Please, someone to  
start. Someone start, please, guys. Richard. Hi,  Pep. I guess there’s a lot to say about that,  
but what did you make of it? And do you come  away feeling that because you scored so late  
that it’s a good point, or do you come away  frustrated by having the lead and losing it?  
Well, it’s better, the point at that point. And it  would have been better in the game that we needed  
the point. So the game, many things happened.  I think we made, considering the difficulty,  
the opponent incredible, incredible  aggressive. They play. We were there,  
we composed. Our first half was exceptional.  And after that, the second, they make a step  
up. We played in a good process, but not maybe  the intention that we had in the first half. But  
after that, we give away British football, the  first goal. And after the corner was not a corner,  
and they are so good. David Moyes always has  been really good in set pieces. And after that,  
the game was open. They could, in some transition,  have chances. And we had the momentum that we make  
an incredible second goal and the third. The three  goals were outstanding and we take a point. So I  
know it was in our hands. Before that game, it  depends on the goals conceded. Now it’s not so.  
But for responsibility, we have Brentford Saturday  at three and continue, and we’ll see what happens.  
After their equaliser until the third goal, the  game just went a bit crazy. Everything seemed  
to go out of the window. What can the team do  better in those situations to stop that from  
happening? But then also, how much happiness can  you take from the fact that they did manage to  
fight back at the ball? When you equalise, you  had that momentum. We knew you have to win the  
game for the situation there are, how many games  left? And after that, the duels continue to be  
aggressive and make some transitions. The long  balls, they are better with Beto and Barry and  
the second balls, and they win some. They consider  free-kicks and corners, throw-ins, these kind of  
situations. And of course, you go there, you make  decisions a little bit rushed, but it’s normal  
because emotions are there. But at the same time,  without that emotion, you cannot come back, you  
cannot score goals. If you are really, really give  up and you think, I die, I die, you cannot do what  
you have done. Pep, what did you make of Michael  Keane’s challenge in the second half? What can I  
say? Yellow card. Do you think, in 15 seconds,  without waiting to come back? Do you think it  
should have been red? It’s not my job. Hi, Pep.  We saw a couple of individual errors which have  
been uncharacteristic from this team, I think it  was Marc Guehi, I guess, being the most obvious,  
giving away a goal. How much did the pressure of  everything that’s going on, in terms of knowing  
you’ve got to win these finals, play in those? Do  you think, for the way we played, especially in  
the first half and come back? Not at all. We know  everybody, we are adults enough to know what they  
have to do. This stadium is not easy, never  has been Everton. So they have made a really,  
really good season, and I think they defend really  well and leave always one player, the other one.  
Their geography is so close and they defending  by line, six, seven players in the crosses,  
and Tarkowski and Keane never shoots the cross.  Always they are there. The gaps between central  
defenders and full-backs always occupied for the  holding midfielders, that they defend proper,  
the duels. And you know, and after that, the way  Pickford is incredible delivery in the long ball.  
Second ball always happens. They put it there. It  didn’t happen except one action in the first half.  
That means a lot or talks so highly about these  players that we have. And, you know, with eight,  
nine players in the box, not easy. Even for  that, we arrive, we create. Maybe the last pass,  
what happened in the last games. But, yeah, in  the second half, and of course this type of game,  
when you are 10 in the Premier League away and the  position, they make an incredible step up in the  
duels. But always, in the 90 minutes, they were  in that type of game. And that always is normal,  
happened in some moments, that even with that,  yeah, we concede the goals and after that  
we come back. Understandably, there’ll be some  frustration and disappointment among your players.  
What do you say to them to keep them on course to  challenge in this title race? Because obviously  
you have to win them. I said how good they are,  how they fought all the time. And Brentford,  
recover and go for them. And after Crystal  Palace and FA Cup final, and game by game,  
will happen with everyone. Because the guys  who came from the bench, they make very,  
very good things and see what happens. Hi, Pep.  Speaking about what happened, obviously this game  
is so meaningful because you lost points. How  do you keep the message that you now have to  
give even more, do even a better effort than you  did so far? Better effort cannot be possible.  
The message is the same like day before. So have  five games left, four games now. Lose the finals,  
win the games. So that is the same message,  and we play for that. Even the difficulties,  
for many, many reasons, we do that. Hi, Pep. If  you hadn’t scored that last-minute goal, Arsenal  
could have afforded to draw a game in these last  three and still win the league. How important do  
you think that is, to put that pressure on them,  that they still have to win the three games? They  
have pressure, they have to win our games. So  now it’s in our hands. If they win all the games,  
the title will be for Arsenal. So what we have  to do is win our game, next one, recover well and  
have to have a series of games, three days, three  days, three days, and this is what you have to do.  
Hi, Pep. Jeremy Doku scored two brilliant goals  today, kind of curled it into that top right-hand  
corner. He’s done that a few times this season  as well. What did you make of his performance  
today? He made a step up with that. Have a  lot of confidence with that. Winning games,  
start to be a winning player. Of course, always  have been incredible, the numbers and athletes.  
So in the final third, I’ll drop them. They need  two or three players to help them and after that,  
the other ones. And maybe we miss the last pass,  but we arrived there many times in that game.  
You need also, for example, the goal from Nico  and Southampton, the draw match, one guy can go  
there the second half and shoot. But even the  second half, we start really well. We arrived,  
first action, corner. We were there and we make  one shot from Bernardo for deflection. There the  
ball goes there with Nico. We were there. After,  we give away two or three balls, it looks like,  
oh, what happened? At the end, you can lose two  or three balls. So it’s not that after the goal,  
the momentum they have in the Premier League  will happen, and our situations. But at the end  
we come back. Last one here, thank you. Pep,  in your pre-match press conference, you made  
a point of saying how much you enjoyed Goodison  Park. You thought it was cool, so British. What  
were your thoughts of playing at the new stadium  for the first time? Beautiful. Congratulations.  
They are rich. Did it have the same kind of  atmosphere for you coming here? Yeah, quite  
similar. They were proper. Yeah, proper English  football, English game. Yeah, yeah, proper,  
really, really good. So, yeah, the main game,  definitely. Thank you. You’re welcome. Thank you.
title: Pep Guardiola post-match press conference | Everton 3-3 Manchester City | Premier League
